title: AN ORDINANCE PROMOTING ORGANIC AGRICULTURE, REGULATING AGRICULTURAL CHEMICAL APPLICATION, AND PRESCRIBING LOCAL BUFFER ZONES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Agriculture and Food, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in (Binding Perforation), Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Davao City Organic Farming and Agricultural Buffer Zone Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard short title provision containing no operative commands or prohibitions.

sections.text: It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to promote sustainable agriculture, protect ecological balance, and safeguard public health from harmful agrochemicals pursuant to Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 and Republic Act No. 10068.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Republic Act No. 10068 §2
sections.legal_rationale: Directly invokes and aligns with the statutory general welfare clause and national organic agriculture policy.

sections.text: The provisions of this Ordinance shall be liberally construed in favor of environmental conservation and the general welfare of the inhabitants of Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard interpretive canon reflecting Section 5(a) of RA 7160.

sections.text: For purposes of this Ordinance, 'Organic Agriculture' shall refer to all agricultural systems that promote the environmentally, socially, and economically sound production of food and fibers. 'Buffer Zone' shall refer to an identified strip of land separating agricultural plantations from residential communities.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitional section adapting national statutory definitions without contradiction.

sections.text: Agricultural landholders who transition at least twenty percent (20%) of their cultivable land to certified organic farming practices shall be eligible for a fifteen percent (15%) local real property tax rebate for three (3) consecutive years, subject to verification by the City Agriculturist Office.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 10068 §24; Republic Act No. 7160 §192
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of municipal taxing power to grant local tax exemptions and incentives to promote national organic agriculture policy.

sections.text: All commercial agricultural landholdings adjacent to established residential subdivisions, public schools, or inland water bodies shall maintain a vegetated buffer zone of not less than thirty (30) meters from the plantation boundary, planted with multi-layered canopy trees.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal zoning and police power regulation establishing physical safety setbacks within local jurisdiction.

sections.text: No agricultural entity, corporation, or individual shall apply, disseminate, or spray any chemical pesticide, fungicide, or herbicide by means of aircraft, drones, or any aerial dispersal apparatus anywhere within the territorial boundaries of Davao City, regardless of national licenses or permits issued by the Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1144 §6; Presidential Decree No. 1144 §9
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Presidential Decree No. 1144 which vests exclusive regulatory authority over pesticide licensing, dispersal methods, and chemical approval in the national Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority (FPA). Struck down in Mosqueda v. PBGEA (2016) under the Magtajas doctrine.

sections.text: Ground application of registered agricultural chemicals must comply strictly with manufacturer dilution ratios and wind-speed thresholds prescribed by national agricultural standards.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local enforcement requiring compliance with national chemical safety standards.

sections.text: There is hereby created the Davao City Agrochemical Monitoring Task Force headed by the City Agriculturist with representatives from the City Health Office and accredited farmer cooperatives.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Internal municipal administrative tasking authorized under Section 454 of RA 7160.

sections.text: Any person or corporate officer found guilty of violating Section 6 or Section 8 shall be punished by a fine of Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) or imprisonment for not more than one (1) year, or both, at the discretion of the court.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Statutorily compliant penalty within the exact maximum penalty ceiling of P5,000 fine and 1-year imprisonment for cities.

sections.text: The amount necessary for the initial implementation of this Ordinance shall be charged against the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the remainder of this Ordinance shall not be affected thereby.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard legislative boilerplate preserving non-offending provisions.

sections.text: All prior city ordinances, executive orders, and administrative regulations inconsistent with this Ordinance are hereby modified or repealed accordingly.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect thirty (30) days after its publication in two (2) newspapers of general circulation within the City of Davao and posting in prominent public places.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard publication and effectivity clause complying with Section 59 of RA 7160.

title: AN ORDINANCE PROHIBITING SMOKING AND VAPING IN ENCLOSED PUBLIC SPACES, REQUIRING HEALTH WARNINGS, AND PRESCRIBING LOCAL ENFORCEMENT PROTOCOLS IN DAVAO CITY

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known as the 'Davao City Comprehensive Clean Air and Anti-Smoking Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: It is the policy of Davao City to guarantee the right of all citizens to breathe clean air and to reduce exposure to second-hand tobacco smoke and vapor aerosols pursuant to Republic Act No. 8749 and Republic Act No. 9211.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 8749 §2; Republic Act No. 9211 §2
sections.legal_rationale: Valid alignment with Clean Air Act and Tobacco Regulation Act.

sections.text: 'Public Conveyance' refers to any vehicle available to the public for transportation. 'Enclosed Area' refers to an area covered by a roof or enclosed by two or more walls. 'Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS)' refers to vapor products.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Smoking and vaping are strictly prohibited in all enclosed public places, government buildings, healthcare institutions, and educational facilities throughout the City.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 9211 §5; Republic Act No. 11900 §12
sections.legal_rationale: Directly implements national statutory indoor smoking ban.

sections.text: Designated smoking and vaping areas must be located in outdoor open spaces at least ten (10) meters away from building entrances, exits, and air intake ducts.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal police power adaptation specifying local physical setbacks for DSAs.

sections.text: All retail establishments licensed to sell tobacco or vapor products shall display conspicuous signage stating that sales to persons below twenty-one (21) years of age are unlawful.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Echoes mandatory minimum age warning requirements under RA 11900.

sections.sec_title: SEARCH AND CONFISCATION IN PRIVATE CONVEYANCES
sections.text: Authorized local traffic enforcers and police officers are hereby empowered to stop, enter, search, and seize without judicial warrant any private motor vehicle operating on city streets to inspect for smoking passengers.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution Art. III §2; Republic Act No. 4136 §5
sections.legal_rationale: Violates constitutional search and seizure protections and national land transportation limits; local police cannot conduct warrantless searches of private vehicles without probable cause.

sections.text: Any person caught smoking within any prohibited zone shall suffer imprisonment for a fixed term of two (2) years and six (6) months, with no option for bail or probation.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts the express statutory ceiling of Section 458(a)(1)(iii) of RA 7160, which limits the penal power of city sanggunians to a maximum imprisonment of one (1) year.

sections.text: The Davao City Anti-Smoking Task Force shall oversee enforcement, maintain statistical records, and conduct public awareness drives in all barangays.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: First-time individual offenders unable to pay administrative fines may perform eight (8) hours of community environmental service under the supervision of the City Environment and Natural Resources Office.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Proprietors and building managers must post standard 'No Smoking' notices and ensure compliance within their premises.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The sum of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00) is hereby allocated from the City Annual Budget for operational expenses and educational campaigns.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: If any section or part of this Ordinance is declared unconstitutional or invalid, other sections shall remain in effect.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All prior city ordinances inconsistent with this Ordinance are hereby repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after complete publication in a local newspaper of general circulation.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING SPEED LIMITS, DESIGNATING ACTIVE MOBILITY CORRIDORS, AND ESTABLISHING TRAFFIC SAFETY STANDARDS IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Transportation and Communications, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be cited as the 'Davao City Speed Limit and Active Mobility Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government adopts a Safe Systems approach to urban mobility, prioritizing pedestrian safety and accident reduction across all thoroughfares.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: 'Urban Road' refers to municipal streets within the poblacion. 'National Highway' refers to primary arterial thoroughfares connecting Davao City to neighboring provinces. 'Active Mobility' refers to cycling and pedestrian transport.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Vehicles traversing local municipal roads and crowded school zones shall observe a maximum speed of thirty (30) kilometers per hour.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 4136 §35(b); Joint DILG-DOTr-DPWH JAO 2018-01
sections.legal_rationale: Valid local speed setting on municipal streets expressly delegated to LGUs under national traffic guidelines.

sections.sec_title: DEDICATED BICYCLE AND ACTIVE MOBILITY LANES
sections.text: The City Transport and Traffic Management Office (CTTMO) shall delineate protected bicycle lanes along major municipal avenues.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal authority to regulate traffic and provide public street lanes.

sections.sec_title: SPEED LIMIT ON NATIONAL ARTERIAL HIGHWAYS
sections.text: All motor vehicles, including provincial buses and inter-regional freight trucks traversing national primary highways passing through Davao City, shall not exceed fifteen (15) kilometers per hour at any time.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 4136 §35; Republic Act No. 4136 §38
sections.legal_rationale: Contradicts Republic Act No. 4136 Section 35 and DPWH arterial speed regulations; local governments cannot impose unreasonable or obstructive speed ceilings on national highways that paralyze national trade.

sections.text: Motorists must yield complete right-of-way to pedestrians crossing marked street intersections and zebra crossings.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Reinforces national statutory pedestrian right-of-way rules.

sections.text: The CTTMO is authorized to deploy calibrated radar speed guns and automated optical speed sensors to document traffic infractions.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Infractions under this Ordinance shall be penalized by administrative citation tickets issued by accredited CTTMO enforcers.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Violators shall pay a fine of P1,000 for the first offense, P2,000 for the second offense, and P5,000 for the third offense.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Fines remain within the statutory limit of P5,000 for cities.

sections.text: All speed detection devices must undergo semi-annual calibration certification by the Department of Science and Technology (DOST).
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Should any provision of this Ordinance be declared void by a competent court, all remaining provisions shall remain valid.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All municipal speed ordinances or executive directives inconsistent herewith are amended or revoked.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect thirty (30) days following publication in two newspapers of general circulation in Region XI.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE STRENGTHENING THE LOCAL PRICE COORDINATING COUNCIL, REGULATING COMMODITY PRICE MONITORING, AND PREVENTING HOARDING DURING CALAMITIES IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Trade, Commerce and Industry, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known as the 'Davao City Fair Price and Calamity Consumer Protection Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government ensures the availability of basic necessities and prime commodities at reasonable prices, protecting consumers from trade malpractices pursuant to Republic Act No. 7581.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly implements the national Price Act policy.

sections.text: The Davao City Local Price Coordinating Council (LPCC) is hereby revitalized, with the City Mayor as Chairman and the DTI Provincial Director as Vice Chairman.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly implements national institutional architecture for local price coordination.

sections.text: Upon declaration of a state of calamity by the Sangguniang Panlungsod, prices of basic necessities shall be automatically frozen at their prevailing market rates.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7581 §6; Republic Act No. 10121 §16
sections.legal_rationale: Echoes mandatory statutory price freeze triggered by LGU state of calamity declaration.

sections.text: 'Basic Necessities' shall include rice, corn, bread, fresh fish, pork, beef, poultry, vegetables, root crops, fresh milk, cooking oil, salt, laundry soap, and medicines.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Mayor, by executive order, is hereby authorized to unilaterally fix and mandate price ceilings on all manufactured consumer goods at fifty percent (50%) below the Suggested Retail Price (SRP) issued by the Department of Trade and Industry, without presidential approval or emergency proclamation.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 7581 Section 7, which reserves the power to mandate price ceilings strictly to the President of the Philippines upon recommendation of the implementing agency.

sections.sec_title: INSPECTION OF WAREHOUSES AND RETAIL OUTLETS
sections.text: Authorized joint inspection teams of the LPCC and DTI may conduct periodic inspections of commercial storage facilities to verify inventory logs.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: No retail or wholesale merchant shall accumulate goods in excess of normal inventory to corner the market or sell above prevailing price freezes.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Merchants proven to engage in illegal hoarding during a declared state of calamity shall face immediate cancellation of their Mayor's Business Permit.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Violators shall be subject to an administrative fine of P5,000.00 and suspension of business operations for not more than six (6) months.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The invalidity of any provision shall not invalidate the other portions hereof.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All ordinances in conflict with this enactment are hereby repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon its approval.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE MANDATING CLOSED-CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) INSTALLATION IN COMMERCIAL PREMISES AND ESTABLISHING SECURITY DATA PROTOCOLS IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Public Safety and Security, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known as the 'Davao City Mandatory Commercial CCTV and Security Surveillance Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government exercises its police power to preserve public order, enhance crime detection, and protect commercial establishments through modern surveillance technologies under Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of police power for crime prevention under the general welfare clause.

sections.text: All banks, shopping malls, supermarkets, pawnshops, money-transfer stations, hotels, fuel stations, and private educational institutions operating within the City shall install functional CCTV systems.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Aligns with national DILG guidelines on mandatory business CCTV requirements.

sections.text: Surveillance cameras must possess a minimum resolution of 1080p, night vision capability, and a minimum continuous recording retention capacity of not less than thirty (30) calendar days.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Standard technical specifications for evidentiary reliability.

sections.text: 'Biometric Data' refers to physiological characteristics used for identification. 'Personal Data' refers to information from which the identity of an individual is apparent. 'CCTV' refers to closed-circuit television.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.sec_title: MANDATORY PUBLIC BROADCAST OF REAL-TIME PRIVATE FEEDS
sections.text: All covered private business entities must connect their internal security cameras directly to a publicly accessible municipal cloud portal, transmitting unredacted, unencrypted real-time facial recognition data of all customers without individual consent or National Privacy Commission clearance.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 10173 §11; Republic Act No. 10173 §12; NPC Circular No. 16-01
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Republic Act No. 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012) principles of transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality, and breaches constitutional privacy guarantees by publishing unredacted surveillance feeds without consent.

sections.text: The City Government shall retain all captured facial recognition logs and customer movement records permanently in perpetuity, prohibiting any citizen from requesting data deletion or rectification.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 10173 §16; Republic Act No. 10173 §18
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts the statutory Rights of the Data Subject under Section 16 of RA 10173, including the right to erasure, blocking, and data minimization.

sections.text: Inspection and certification of CCTV functionality by the City Engineers Office shall be a mandatory prerequisite for the renewal of Mayor's Business Permits.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Valid regulatory condition precedent for municipal business licensing.

sections.text: Each commercial establishment shall designate a Compliance Officer responsible for safeguarding stored recordings against unauthorized dissemination.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Failure to install functional CCTVs within ninety (90) days from notice shall result in a fine of P5,000.00 and suspension of business permit.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Necessary funds for city monitoring terminals shall be allocated from the annual executive budget.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: If any provision is declared unconstitutional, the rest shall remain operative.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All prior conflicting city orders and resolutions are hereby revoked.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect thirty (30) days after publication.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING SINGLE-USE PLASTICS, ENFORCING SOURCE SEGREGATION, AND ADVANCING CIRCULAR WASTE MANAGEMENT IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known as the 'Davao City Ecological Solid Waste Management and Plastic Regulation Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government commits to systemic ecological solid waste management, waste minimization, and resource recovery pursuant to Republic Act No. 9003 and Republic Act No. 11898.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 9003 §2; Republic Act No. 11898 §2
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious adoption of national solid waste management and extended producer responsibility policies.

sections.text: 'Single-Use Plastics' refers to disposable plastic items designed for one-time use before disposal. 'Source Segregation' refers to the sorting of solid waste at the household level.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All households, commercial establishments, and public institutions must segregate solid waste into biodegradable, recyclable, non-recyclable, and special hazardous waste categories prior to collection.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly implements the mandatory source segregation requirement of RA 9003.

sections.text: Each of the 182 barangays of Davao City shall establish and operate a dedicated Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) or cluster MRF for recyclable and biodegradable composting.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly enforces the statutory mandate under Section 32 of RA 9003 requiring barangay-level MRFs.

sections.sec_title: PHASE-OUT OF PLASTIC BAGS IN COMMERCE
sections.text: Commercial groceries and department stores are prohibited from distributing non-biodegradable single-use checkout plastic bags, encouraging reusable shopping bags.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(1)(vi); Republic Act No. 9003 §48
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal police power regulating commercial packaging for environmental sanitation.

sections.sec_title: MUNICIPAL IMPORT BARRICADE AND CARGO FORFEITURE
sections.text: The City Government shall establish checkpoints at the Port of Davao to inspect, intercept, confiscate, and destroy all international cargo shipments of plastic polymers imported under national customs clearance.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution Art. XII §1; Republic Act No. 10863 §200; Republic Act No. 10863 §300
sections.legal_rationale: Contradicts the exclusive jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs under Republic Act No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act); municipal councils have no constitutional power over international trade and customs clearance.

sections.text: Any individual resident found possessing a single-use plastic straw or fork shall be assessed an administrative fine of Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) and three (3) years imprisonment.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.legal_rationale: Blatantly violates Section 458(a)(1)(iii) of RA 7160 which limits city sanggunian penalties to a maximum of P5,000 fine and 1-year imprisonment.

sections.text: Waste collection trucks shall strictly collect segregated biodegradables on designated days and non-biodegradables on alternate days.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) shall conduct information campaigns in all public schools regarding waste reduction.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Private recycling firms may register with CENRO for preferred participation in municipal resource-recovery programs.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Funds for the support of barangay MRFs shall be incorporated into the annual statutory ecological fund.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: If any clause is held unconstitutional, other clauses remain valid.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Inconsistent local enactments are repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance takes effect thirty (30) days from publication.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE ERECTION, INSTALLATION, AND MAINTENANCE OF OUTDOOR BILLBOARDS AND SIGNAGE IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Housing and Urban Development, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be cited as the 'Davao City Signage and Outdoor Advertising Safety Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government exercises its police power to preserve structural safety, traffic sightlines, and aesthetic order from hazardously situated outdoor signage under Section 458(a)(4)(iv) of Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly invokes explicit city council authority to regulate outdoor advertising signs (affirmed in Evasco v. Montañez, 2018).

sections.text: 'Billboard' refers to any off-premise advertising sign. 'Signage' refers to any identification banner or emblem visible from a public street.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All free-standing billboards must maintain a minimum setback of five (5) meters from road right-of-way boundaries and must not obstruct street traffic lights.
sections.label: Entailment

sections.text: No billboard structure along the scenic coastal and mountain corridors shall exceed eighteen (18) meters in total height measured from ground elevation.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid local police power zoning limitation preserving sightlines.

sections.text: Billboards erected by registered local municipal businesses are hereby declared exempt from the structural design computations, wind load testing, and building permit requirements of the National Building Code of the Philippines (Presidential Decree No. 1096), requiring only a Barangay Clearance.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1096 §301; Presidential Decree No. 1096 §302
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Presidential Decree No. 1096 (National Building Code) Section 301; a municipal ordinance cannot exempt physical commercial structures from national structural safety permits.

sections.text: Digital LED billboards must incorporate auto-dimming mechanisms to reduce glaring illumination during nighttime hours between 10:00 PM and 5:00 AM.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid traffic safety regulation under general welfare police power.

sections.text: The City Building Official shall maintain an updated geo-referenced inventory of all permitted outdoor signs in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Signage abandoned for more than six (6) months or posing imminent danger of collapse shall be dismantled after due notice.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Annual regulatory inspection fees shall be collected based on total display square meterage.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal regulatory fee under RA 7160 Section 147.

sections.text: Violators shall be fined P5,000.00 and ordered to dismantle unauthorized structures within ten (10) calendar days.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The declaration of unconstitutionality of any provision shall not impair other sections.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Conflicting local measures are hereby repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after publication.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING COMMERCIAL SAND AND GRAVEL EXTRACTION, SAFEGUARDING RIVERBANKS, AND ESTABLISHING QUARRY PERMITTING IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be cited as the 'Davao City Sustainable Quarrying and River Protection Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government balances local construction material needs with ecological preservation of vital river ecosystems under Republic Act No. 7942 and Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7942 §43; Republic Act No. 7160 §16
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious balance of quarrying regulation with national mining statute.

sections.text: 'Quarry Resources' refers to common rocks, sand, gravel, and earth materials. 'Commercial Sand and Gravel Permit' refers to a license granted for extraction not exceeding five (5) hectares.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Adapts national definitions from RA 7942 Section 43.

sections.text: Extraction of sand and gravel is strictly prohibited within one hundred (100) meters upstream and downstream of any bridge, water intake, or public flood control structure.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1067 §51; Republic Act No. 7942 §43
sections.legal_rationale: Implements national Water Code river protection setbacks.

sections.text: Commercial quarry permits within five (5) hectares shall be evaluated by the City Mining Regulatory Board (CMRB) and approved by the City Mayor.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7076 §24; Republic Act No. 7942 §43
sections.legal_rationale: Follows the exact statutory delegation under Section 43 of RA 7942.

sections.text: The Sangguniang Panlungsod is hereby empowered to issue local extraction permits for heavy metallic minerals (including nickel, copper, and gold) across ancestral domain lands, authorizing direct commercial export overseas without securing a Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) from the DENR or clearance from the NCIP.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution Art. XII §2; Republic Act No. 7942 §27; Republic Act No. 8371 §59
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates the Regalian Doctrine (State ownership of metallic mineral resources), Republic Act No. 7942 which reserves mineral agreements strictly to national DENR authority, and Republic Act No. 8371 (IPRA) Free Prior Informed Consent mandates.

sections.text: All trucks transporting quarried aggregates within Davao City must carry a valid Delivery Receipt issued by the City Environment Office indicating the volume and extraction site.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Permittees shall post an environmental rehabilitation deposit prior to the commencement of extraction operations.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: No quarrying operations shall be conducted between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Local police power operating hours regulation.

sections.text: Illegal extraction shall result in a fine of P5,000.00 and impoundment of transport vehicles.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Invalidity of any section shall not affect other portions.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All inconsistent local rules are repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance takes effect thirty (30) days from publication.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING TELECOMMUNICATIONS CABLE INSTALLATIONS, UNDERGROUND UTILITY DUCTS, AND RESTORATION OF PUBLIC ROADS IN DAVAO CITY
committee: Committee on Public Works and Telecommunications, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be cited as the 'Davao City Telecommunications Infrastructure and Underground Cabling Ordinance of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government ensures public road safety, prevents aerial cable clutter, and coordinates telecommunications infrastructure pursuant to Republic Act No. 7925 and Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7925 §4; Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(5)(vi)
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal police power over city roads and utilities.

sections.text: 'Public Telecommunications Entity' refers to any entity authorized to provide public telecommunications services. 'Excavation Permit' refers to an authorization to dig public streets.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All telecommunications utilities undertaking street excavation for fiber optic installation must obtain an Excavation Permit from the City Engineer and post a performance restoration bond.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Direct municipal authority to regulate street digging and ensure road repair.

sections.sec_title: UNDERGROUND CABLING MANDATE IN HERITAGE ZONES
sections.text: All overhead aerial power and telecommunications cables within the designated downtown historical and commercial zones must be placed underground within three (3) years.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid local zoning and public safety measure.

sections.sec_title: LOCAL LEGISLATIVE FRANCHISE REQUIREMENT FOR WIRELESS CARRIERS
sections.text: No public telecommunications entity holding a national legislative franchise from the Congress of the Philippines shall transmit wireless cellular signals or operate frequency transmitters within Davao City without first obtaining a separate secondary legislative franchise approved by the Sangguniang Panlungsod.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7925 §5; Republic Act No. 7925 §21; Presidential Decree No. 576-A §1
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 7925 which vests exclusive regulatory authority over wireless frequencies and national telecommunications carriers in the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC). Confirmed in Batangas CATV v. CA (2004) under the preemption doctrine.

sections.sec_title: UNILATERAL RATE REGULATION OF INTERNET SERVICES
sections.text: The Sangguniang Panlungsod shall fix the maximum retail subscription tariffs that mobile telephone carriers may charge individual subscribers residing within Davao City.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7925 §17; 1987 Constitution Art. XII §19
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Section 17 of Republic Act No. 7925, which reserves the regulation and deregulation of telecommunication tariffs exclusively to the NTC.

sections.text: Cellular operators are encouraged to utilize shared passive infrastructure and co-locate on authorized common cellular towers.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Parallels national DICT common tower policy.

sections.text: Excavated road trenches must be restored to original asphalt or concrete specifications within forty-eight (48) hours of cable laying.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Telecommunications Infrastructure Coordinating Committee shall coordinate all scheduled road works to prevent duplicate street diggings.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Unauthorized excavation or failure to restore roads shall be penalized by a fine of P5,000.00 and forfeiture of the restoration bond.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Invalidity of any section shall not affect the remaining portions.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: All prior conflicting municipal measures are repealed.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance takes effect thirty (30) days from publication.
sections.label: Neutral

title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE REVENUE CODE OF DAVAO CITY, REGULATING BUSINESS TAX ON COMMERCIAL ENTERPRISES, AND PRESCRIBING LOCAL TAX ADMINISTRATION
committee: Committee on Ways and Means, Sangguniang Panlungsod

physical_specs.paper_size: Legal / Folio (8.5 x 13.0 inches / 215.9 x 330.2 mm)
physical_specs.margins: Top 1.0 in, Bottom 1.0 in, Left 1.5 in, Right 1.0 in
physical_specs.typography: 12pt Arial, 1.5 line spacing, formal section bold caps
physical_specs.enacting_clause: BE IT ORDAINED BY THE SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF DAVAO CITY, IN SESSION ASSEMBLED

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known as the 'Davao City Revenue Code Amendment on Commercial Business Taxation of 2026'.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Government exercises its constitutional power to create its own sources of revenue, ensuring fair taxation within statutory limits under Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution Art. X §5; Republic Act No. 7160 §129
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of constitutional and statutory local taxing authority.

sections.text: 'Business' refers to commercial activity for profit. 'Gross Sales or Receipts' refers to the total amount received from merchandise sales or services.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.sec_title: GRADUATED BUSINESS TAX ON RETAIL MERCHANTS
sections.text: Retail merchants with gross sales exceeding Four Hundred Thousand Pesos (P400,000.00) shall pay a local business tax not exceeding one percent (1%) of gross annual receipts.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly complies with the statutory business tax ceiling for cities under Section 143(a) of RA 7160.

sections.sec_title: TAX ON FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND BANKS
sections.text: Commercial banks, banking institutions, and offshore banking units authorized by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas shall be assessed a business tax of fifty percent (50%) of one percent (1%) on gross receipts.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Directly implements statutory tax rate on licensed banks under RA 7160 Section 143(f).

sections.sec_title: BUSINESS TAX ON CORPORATE HOLDING DIVIDENDS
sections.text: All corporate holding companies owning shares in manufacturing or utility firms are hereby classified as 'Non-Bank Financial Intermediaries' and shall pay a two percent (2%) local business tax on all passive dividend earnings and interest income received from corporate stock holdings, regardless of whether the holding company is licensed as a financial intermediary by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §133(a); Republic Act No. 7160 §143(f); Republic Act No. 8791 §3
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 7160 Section 133(a) (prohibiting local taxes on income) and Section 143(f) in relation to General Banking Law. Invalidated in City of Davao and Tanjili v. ARC Investors, Inc. (G.R. No. 249668, 2022).

sections.sec_title: RETROACTIVE IMPOSITION ON GOVERNMENT PENSION PROPERTIES
sections.text: Real properties and facilities titled under the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and Social Security System (SSS) located in Davao City are hereby assessed real property taxes retroactively for ten (10) past calendar years, authorizing the City Treasurer to levy on execution.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §133(o); Republic Act No. 8291 §39; Presidential Decree No. 1146 §33
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Section 133(o) of RA 7160 and national agency charters which explicitly exempt government instrumentalities and social security funds from local taxation. Invalidated in City of Davao v. GSIS (G.R. No. 127383, 2005).

sections.text: Telecommunications utilities operating within Davao City shall be subject to a local franchise tax of one-half of one percent (0.5%) on their gross annual receipts pursuant to Section 137 of Republic Act No. 7160.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §137; Republic Act No. 7160 §151
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local franchise taxing power explicitly affirmed by the Supreme Court in Smart Communications v. City of Davao (2008) and PLDT v. City of Davao (2001).

sections.text: Local business taxes shall be payable for every calendar quarter, with a ten percent (10%) discount for full advance annual payments made before January 20.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: The City Treasurer or duly designated deputies may examine the accounting books and records of businesses operating within the city to verify tax payments.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Statutory authority to inspect commercial books under Section 171 of RA 7160.

sections.text: Failure to pay taxes on time shall incur a surcharge of twenty-five percent (25%) and interest of two percent (2%) per month.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: If any provision is declared void, remaining provisions shall stay effective.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: Provisions of the 2005 Revenue Code inconsistent herewith are amended.
sections.label: Neutral

sections.text: This Ordinance takes effect on January 1 of the following calendar year after publication.
sections.label: Neutral
